newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Political violence in Cambodia city leaves one dead.
newsitem.headline: Political violence in Cambodia city leaves one dead.

text.p: A force of 5,000 government troops was called in to restore peace in Cambodia's second largest city of Battambang after violence flared between soldiers loyal to rival political parties, a local official said on Saturday.

Serey Kosal, deputy governor of Battambang, said he ordered that the city about 300 km (188 miles) northwest of the capital Phnom Penh be sealed off to stem further violence. One soldier has been killed in the clashes.
The official told Reuters he had appealed to Cambodian co-Premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen to support him if tensions between the leaders' two parties result in additional fighting.
"I have asked the government for the legal right to fight back in order to protect the government, nation, religion and king," Serey Kosal, speaking from Battambang, said.
"It is very tense here," he said.

Serey Kosal, a member of the royalist FUNCINPEC party, said the violence erupted on Friday when soldiers loyal to Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party (CPP) tried to confiscate weapons from forces loyal to FUNCINPEC troops under Ranariddh.
FUNCINPEC soldiers shot and killed a CPP soldier and wounded an unspecified number of CPP soldiers, Serey Kosal said.
Afterward, two CPP soldiers were arrested but they were later released.
CPP officials in Battambang could not be reached for comment.
Tensions between the two prime ministers have been escalating in recent weeks and were further heightened on Tuesday when Hun Sen's brother-in-law was killed by an unidentified gunman in the capital.
